interactionPlan.concept: Discrete-time sinusoids are defined by the integer ratio of cycles $k$ to the window size $N$, which governs both their local sample patterns and global periodicity.
learningObjectives: Understand how the frequency index $k$ corresponds to the exact number of sinusoidal cycles completed over a discrete window of size $N$.
Explain why a discrete sinusoid's samples do not repeat identically in each cycle when $k/N$ is an irreducible fraction, despite the overall wave having a period of $N$.
Observe and explain discrete-time aliasing and symmetry, demonstrating why frequencies $k$ and $N-k$ produce identical (cosine) or inverted (sine) sample sequences.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: A discrete wave can complete exactly $k$ cycles in $N$ steps, but because samples must lie on an integer grid, the individual sample values only repeat cycle-to-cycle if $N$ is perfectly divisible by $k$; otherwise, the exact pattern only repeats every $N$ samples.

interactions.label: Frequency (k)
interactions.effect: Changes the number of cycles $k$ within the $N$-sample block. Updates the plotted stem points and the underlying continuous sinusoidal guides.
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates how increasing $k$ increases the spatial frequency, and reveals folding/aliasing as $k$ exceeds $N/2 = 10$ (where $k=11$ mirrors $k=9$).

interactions.label: Window Size (N)
interactions.effect: Adjusts the total number of samples $N$ shown on the x-axis, altering the discrete grid spacing.
interactions.teaches: Shows how the divisibility of $N$ by $k$ determines whether the individual cycle samples repeat identically or vary dynamically across cycles.

interactions.label: Signal Mode
interactions.effect: Switches the display between Cosine, Sine, or Side-by-Side views.
interactions.teaches: Illustrates the phase relationship between sine (starting at 0) and cosine (starting at 1) on a discrete grid.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The visualization should consist of two side-by-side stem plots: Cosine on the left, Sine on the right, mirroring the layout of the static figure. Each plot features a horizontal axis representing sample index $n$ (ranging from $0$ to $N$, with ticks at $0$, $N/2$, and $N$) and a vertical axis representing amplitude from $-1$ to $1$. Blue stem lines with circular markers represent the discrete samples. A faint, light-gray continuous curve should be drawn underneath the stems to help students trace the parent continuous sinusoid. Dynamic LaTeX mathematical labels at the top of each plot should update to show the current formula, e.g., $\cos(\frac{2\pi}{20} 3 n)$ when $k=3, N=20$.
